benchmark_name: Benchmarking Vision-Language and Multimodal LLMs on Christian Iconography (ArtDL, ICONCLASS, Wikidata saint classification)
humanities_role_explanation: Items are paintings of Christian saints classified with Iconclass codes; the task targets iconographic classification, a core art-historical competence, for metadata curation in digital humanities.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Painting images are paired with text prompts listing class names or Iconclass descriptions (and few-shot labelled exemplars). The CSV metadata lists text only, but images are the primary stimulus.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label classification of Christian saints (10 classes per dataset) in paintings, framed as iconography classification with Iconclass codes; essentially recognition of which saint is depicted, from labels, Iconclass descriptions, or few-shot exemplars.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to single-label Christian saint iconography classification.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 2.5 Flash, plus CLIP and SigLIP variants.

quantitative_metrics.note: Accuracy and cross-dataset prediction consistency; ResNet50 baselines.

summary: The paper benchmarks CLIP/SigLIP and multimodal LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini 2.5) on single-label classification of Christian saints across three Iconclass-based datasets, under zero-shot with labels, zero-shot with Iconclass descriptions, and few-shot settings. LLMs beat fine-tuned ResNet50 baselines on ArtDL and ICONCLASS, while SigLIP does best on Wikidata.
key_findings: Gemini-2.5 Pro reaches 90.45% on ArtDL and about 84-85% on ICONCLASS; on Wikidata SigLIP-so400m is best (66.29%) and LLMs fall to about 45%. Class descriptions generally help zero-shot; few-shot mostly lowers accuracy. LLMs show low cross-dataset consistency (25-33%) vs. contrastive models. Possible training contamination on ArtDL/ICONCLASS is noted.
gold_upstream: ArtDL (Milani and Fraternali) test set, ICONCLASS AI Test Set (Posthumus), and Wikidata Iconclass-coded paintings; this paper says only that images are annotated with Iconclass codes, and metadata is 'usually created by domain experts'.
facets_explanation: Labels are Iconclass codes already attached to ArtDL, the ICONCLASS AI Test Set and Wikidata; the authors filtered to the top 10 classes and removed multi-label images. Identifying the saint requires iconographic knowledge not given in the image itself (except in the description condition). Each image has a single label scored by exact match.
results_explanation: Best headline: Gemini-2.5 Pro 90.45% accuracy on ArtDL Test 1. Largest within-model input gap: siglip-base-patch16-512 on ArtDL rises from 48.71% (Test 1) to 68.19% (Test 2) (about 19.5 points), and siglip-large-patch16-384 from 54.45% to 72.21%; the largest is clip-vit-large-patch14 on ArtDL, 30.58% to 44.31% (13.7), but siglip-base on Wikidata drops 57.47% to 46.94%. The largest observed is siglip-base ArtDL 48.71 to 68.19 = 19.48, rounded to 19; ICONCLASS siglip-base 43.51 vs others smaller. No human baseline reported. Evaluation set size is the ArtDL test set of 1,864 images; the dataset total is 1,864 + 863 + 718 = 3,445.
